recipes.title: Tuscan Lemon Chicken Piccata
recipes.description: Golden chicken cutlets in a bright lemon, garlic and caper sauce. Serve with roasted asparagus or a little angel hair pasta.
ingredients: ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped, plus more to garnish

steps.text: Slice each breast in half horizontally to make 8 thin cutlets. Season both sides with the salt, pepper and Italian seasoning, then dredge lightly in flour, shaking off any excess.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets in batches, 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (165°F inside). Move to a plate and tent loosely with foil.
Lower the heat to medium and melt the butter in the same skillet. Stir in the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Pour in the broth and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits from the pan. Stir in the capers and lemon zest and simmer 3–4 minutes, until slightly reduced.
Return the chicken and any juices to the skillet and spoon the sauce over the top. Simmer for 2 minutes to warm through.
Scatter with parsley and a few extra lemon slices. Lovely with roasted asparagus, a green salad or angel hair pasta.

recipes.kitchenNote: Squeeze the lemons fresh and add a little extra zest at the very end. Leftover sauce is wonderful tossed through a bowl of buttered pasta the next day.

recipes.title: Blueberry Buttermilk Pancakes
recipes.description: Tall, tender buttermilk pancakes dotted with jammy blueberries. A slow Saturday morning on a plate.
ingredients: 3 Tbsp unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan

steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
In a second bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold with a spatula until just combined. A few lumps are good. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
Warm a griddle or large skillet over medium heat and brush it lightly with butter.
Pour ¼ cup of batter per pancake and scatter a few blueberries on top. Cook 2–3 minutes, until bubbles form and the edges look set, then flip and cook 1–2 minutes more.
Keep finished pancakes in a 200°F oven while you cook the rest. Serve with a pat of butter and warm maple syrup.

recipes.kitchenNote: Don't press the pancakes after flipping. Let them rise on their own. Frozen blueberries work too; add them straight from the freezer so they don't bleed.

recipes.title: Provençal Ratatouille
recipes.description: Summer vegetables cooked one by one, then simmered together with tomato, thyme and good olive oil.
ingredients: 5 Tbsp olive oil, divided, plus more to finish
1 medium eggplant (about 1 lb), cut into ¾-inch cubes
2 medium zucchini, cut into ¾-inch half-moons
1 red and 1 yellow bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
1½ tsp salt, plus more to taste

steps.text: Heat 2 Tbsp of the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant with a pinch of salt and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until golden. Spoon into a bowl.
Add 1 Tbsp oil and the zucchini and cook about 5 minutes, until lightly browned but still firm. Add to the eggplant.
Add the last 2 Tbsp oil, the onion and the peppers. Cook 8–10 minutes over medium heat until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and their juice, the thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Return the eggplant and zucchini to the pot, cover and simmer gently 15–20 minutes, until everything is tender but still holds its shape.
Fish out the bay leaf and thyme stems. Fold in the basil, taste for salt and finish with a thread of olive oil. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.kitchenNote: Ratatouille is even better the next day, so make a big pot. Spoon leftovers over polenta or toast, or bake them with eggs cracked right on top.

recipes.title: Irish Soda Bread
recipes.description: A craggy, golden loaf made with just four ingredients and no yeast. From bowl to oven in ten minutes.
ingredients: 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1¾ cups (420 ml) cold buttermilk, plus a splash more if needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and dust a baking sheet or cast-iron skillet with flour.
Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt together in a large bowl, then make a well in the center.
Pour in most of the buttermilk and stir with a fork or one cupped hand until a soft, shaggy dough forms. Add the rest only if dry flour remains.
Turn the dough onto a floured counter and pat it into a round about 2 inches high. Handle it as little as possible to keep the loaf tender.
Set the round on the sheet and cut a deep cross across the top with a floured knife, almost to the edges, to help it bake through.
Bake 35–40 minutes, until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack, wrapped in a clean tea towel for a softer crust.

recipes.kitchenNote: Granny always said the cross was there to let the fairies out. It's at its best the day it's baked, still a little warm, with plenty of good salted butter.

recipes.title: Grandma's Apple Crumble
recipes.description: Soft cinnamon apples under a buttery oat crumble, baked until bubbling. Pass the custard.

items: 2½ lb tart apples (about 6), peeled, cored and sliced
½ cup (100 g) light brown sugar
½ cup (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cubed
Custard, cream or vanilla ice cream, to serve

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 2-quart baking dish.
In a large bowl, toss the apple slices with the sugar, lemon juice, flour and cinnamon. Tip into the dish and spread them out evenly.
Mix the flour, brown sugar, oats, cinnamon and salt. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture clumps like damp sand with a few larger pebbles.
Scatter the crumble loosely over the apples, right to the edges. Don't press it down; the little gaps let it crisp.
Bake 40–45 minutes, until the top is deep golden and the juices bubble thickly at the edges.
Let it settle for 10 minutes, then spoon into bowls with warm custard, cold cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

recipes.kitchenNote: Use a mix of apples if you can, some sharp and some sweet. A handful of blackberries tucked in with the apples was always Grandma's late-summer secret.

recipes.title: Huevos Rancheros
recipes.description: Crisp-edged fried eggs on warm corn tortillas with black beans and a smoky ranchero sauce. A ranch-hand breakfast worth waking up for.

items: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and warmed

steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and jalapeño for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cumin and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened. Blend briefly if you like it smooth, stir in the lime juice and keep warm.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and brush the tortillas lightly with oil. Fry each for about 30 seconds per side, until soft and blistered. Wrap in a clean towel.
Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining oil. Crack in the eggs and fry for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are fully set and the edges are lacy but the yolks still run.
Overlap two tortillas on each plate, add a spoonful of black beans and top with two eggs. Ladle the warm sauce around the yolks.
Scatter over the avocado, queso fresco and cilantro, and tuck a lime wedge on the side. Serve right away, while the tortillas are warm.

recipes.kitchenNote: Make the sauce the night before; it only gets better. On busy mornings I crack the eggs straight into the simmering sauce, cover the pan, and call it breakfast.

recipes.title: Argentine Beef Empanadas
recipes.description: Flaky hand pies filled with cumin-spiced beef, sweet pepper, egg and olives, crimped by hand and baked until deep golden. Makes 12.

items: 3 cups (375 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
½ cup (113 g) cold unsalted butter or lard, cubed
½ cup (120 ml) cold water, plus 1–2 Tbsp as needed
½ tsp crushed red pepper flakes
¼ cup pitted green olives, chopped

steps.text: Whisk the flour and salt, then rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs. Beat the egg with the water, stir it in, and add more water a spoonful at a time until the dough holds. Wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and red pepper for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and sweet.

Raise the heat to medium-high, add the beef and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left (160°F). Stir in the paprika, cumin, pepper flakes and salt and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the scallions, spread the filling on a plate and chill for 30 minutes, until cold. Warm filling melts the dough and makes the empanadas leak.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line two baking sheets with parchment. Roll the dough out thin, about 3 mm (1/8 inch), and cut 12 rounds about 5 inches across, rerolling the scraps once.

Spoon 2 heaping Tbsp of filling onto each round and top with a little egg and olive. Brush the edge with water, fold into a half-moon and press to seal, then twist the edge into a rope or crimp it with a fork.
Set the empanadas on the sheets, brush with beaten egg and bake for 20–25 minutes, until deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving; the filling is very hot.

recipes.kitchenNote: The twisted rope edge is called the repulgue and takes a few tries; a fork crimp seals just as well. Unbaked empanadas freeze beautifully. Bake from frozen, adding 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
recipes.description: Fluffy rice simmered in coconut milk with red kidney beans, thyme, allspice and a whole Scotch bonnet for fragrance, not fire.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz / 425 g) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 whole Scotch bonnet pepper, left whole

steps.text: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water, swishing it with your hand, until the water runs almost clear. Drain well.
In a heavy pot with a tight lid, combine the coconut milk, water, beans, scallions, garlic, thyme, allspice and salt. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Stir in the rice, then nestle the whole Scotch bonnet on top. Keep it whole and unbroken so it gives perfume without much heat. Return to a boil.
Cover tightly, turn the heat to its lowest setting and cook for 20–25 minutes, without lifting the lid, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes. Lift out the pepper, scallions and thyme stems, then fluff gently with a fork.

recipes.kitchenNote: Sunday dinner always had rice and peas beside it. Lift that Scotch bonnet out carefully: if it bursts, the whole pot turns fiery. Dried beans soaked overnight taste best.

recipes.title: Crusty French Baguettes
recipes.description: Four simple ingredients, a few patient folds and a blast of steam make crackling crusts and open, chewy crumb. Makes 3.
ingredients: Rice flour or semolina, for dusting

steps.text: Stir the flour and water together until no dry flour remains. Cover and let it rest for 30 minutes so the flour can soak up the water.
Sprinkle the yeast and salt over the dough and squeeze them through with a wet hand for 3–4 minutes, until evenly mixed and smooth.
Cover. Every 30 minutes for 2 hours, wet your hand, stretch each side of the dough up and fold it over the top. It will grow airy, smooth and about half again in size.
Tip onto a lightly floured counter, cut into 3 equal pieces and roll each loosely into a short log. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Pat each log flat, fold the top third down and the bottom third up, then fold in half and seal the seam with the heel of your hand. Roll out to 14 inches with tapered ends.

Lay them seam side up in the folds of a well-floured towel. Cover and proof for 45 minutes, until puffy. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 475°F with a baking steel and an empty metal pan on the rack below.

Roll the loaves seam side down onto parchment. Make 4 long, shallow, overlapping slashes with a razor, slide onto the steel, pour the boiling water into the pan and bake for 22–25 minutes, until deep golden.
Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes, listening for the crust crackle. Slicing too soon makes the crumb gummy.

recipes.kitchenNote: Don't fear a dark crust: that is where the flavour lives. Shaping takes practice, so don't worry if your first batch looks rustic; it still tastes like Paris.

recipes.title: Lemon Chicken and Rice
recipes.description: Golden chicken thighs, tender long-grain rice and a squeeze of lemon, all from the same skillet.
ingredients: 1 cup long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Pat the thighs dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a deep, lidded skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 3–4 minutes per side, then transfer it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Stir the onion in the drippings for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and drained rice and stir for 1 minute.

Stir in the broth and lemon zest, scraping the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Nestle in the thighs and any juices, cover, and simmer on low for 18–22 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Take the covered skillet off the heat for 5 minutes. Fluff the rice and finish with lemon juice and parsley.

recipes.kitchenNote: A tight-fitting lid helps the rice cook evenly. Keep it closed until the first check.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken and Wild Rice
recipes.description: A cozy Minnesota-style soup with chicken, wild rice and vegetables in a light cream broth.
ingredients: ¾ cup whole wild rice, rinsed

steps.text: In a soup pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in the thyme.
Stir in the wild rice and broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer partially covered for 30 minutes.

Slip the thighs into the soup and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F. Transfer the thighs to a board and shred. Keep simmering the rice if it needs longer.
Return the chicken to the pot and stir in the half-and-half. Warm gently over low heat and season with salt and pepper.

recipes.kitchenNote: Whole wild rice gives this soup its chewy texture. A wild rice blend will cook faster, so check the package.

recipes.title: Chicken Broccoli Rice Bake
recipes.description: Chicken, broccoli and cooked rice baked in a cheddar sauce with a crisp cracker topping.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Microwave the broccoli with a splash of water for 2 minutes, then drain well.

Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk, broth, salt and pepper. Simmer for 3 minutes while whisking, then remove from the heat and stir in the cheese.
Mix the rice, cooked chicken and broccoli with the sauce. Spread in the baking dish and sprinkle the cracker crumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 22–25 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F and the edges bubble. Let the dish stand briefly before serving.

recipes.kitchenNote: Rotisserie chicken and leftover rice make this a quick dinner.

recipes.title: Penne alla Vodka
recipes.description: Penne coated in a silky tomato and cream sauce with Parmesan and a little red pepper.
ingredients: ¼ tsp crushed red pepper flakes

steps.text: Cook the penne in salted water until just shy of al dente, following the package timing. Save 1 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Soften the shallot for 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic, red pepper and tomato paste and cook for 3–4 minutes, until the paste darkens.
Take the pan off the heat to add the vodka, then return it to the stove. Simmer for 2 minutes, stirring. Stir in the cream and ¼ cup of pasta water over low heat.
Add the penne and simmer for 1 minute, tossing until evenly coated. Remove from the heat and stir in the Parmesan. Add pasta water a splash at a time to loosen the sauce, and salt to taste.

recipes.kitchenNote: Cook the tomato paste until it turns brick red. That extra time gives the sauce a deeper flavor.

recipes.title: Parmesan Mushroom Risotto
recipes.description: Creamy Arborio rice with browned mushrooms, Parmesan and a spoonful of butter.

steps.text: Bring the broth to a gentle simmer in a saucepan, then keep it warm over low heat.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and cook for 7–9 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned. Season with salt and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium and melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in the pan. Soften the onion for 4 minutes, then stir in the rice for 1 minute. Add the wine and stir until mostly absorbed.
Add warm broth a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until most of each ladle is absorbed before adding more. Cook for 18–22 minutes, until the rice is creamy and tender with a slight bite.
Fold in the mushrooms, remaining butter and Parmesan. Loosen with a splash of warm broth if needed and season with pepper. Serve right away.

recipes.kitchenNote: The risotto should settle into the bowl when you spoon it in. Keep a little warm broth handy for the last stir.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Baked Salmon
recipes.description: Salmon baked with lemon, garlic butter and parsley. Good with rice or roast potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment. Zest half the lemon, then cut half into slices and save the rest for squeezing.
Pat the fish dry and set it skin-side down on the pan. Stir together the melted butter, garlic, zest, salt and pepper. Brush it over the fish and lay a lemon slice on each fillet.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F. Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and the chopped parsley.

recipes.kitchenNote: Start checking thin tail pieces early. Pieces of similar thickness will finish together.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Tomatoes
recipes.description: Flaky cod baked over blistered cherry tomatoes, briny olives and garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the tomatoes, olives, garlic and oregano in a baking dish with 1 tablespoon of the oil. Roast for 12 minutes, until the tomatoes start to collapse.
Pat the fillets dry. Rub with the remaining oil and season with salt and pepper. Nestle them between the tomatoes and olives.
Bake for 10–14 minutes, until the thickest part of the cod reaches 145°F. Spoon the juices over the fish and finish with lemon and basil.

recipes.kitchenNote: Serve with bread or a scoop of rice to catch the tomato juices.

recipes.title: Pan-Seared Trout Almondine
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned trout with toasted almonds, browned butter and lemon.

steps.text: Pat the trout dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the fillets skin-side down for 3–4 minutes, working in batches if needed.
Flip each fillet and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F. Transfer the trout to warm plates, skin-side up.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and almonds and stir for 2–3 minutes, until golden. Take the skillet off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and parsley, and spoon the sauce around the trout.

recipes.kitchenNote: Keep the fillets skin-side up after cooking so the skin stays crisp.
